Gomberg was environmentalist, provocateur, and activist who had once served as a councillor in Edmonton and had run for the NDP federally in Montréal. Endorsed by Jane Jacobs, he ran on a platform of increasing the city's powers and resources – an idea picked up by his opponent Mel Lastman.

Hall ran unsuccessfully in 1997 and 2003. She had previously served one term as mayor of the pre-amalgamation City of Toronto and previously as ward councillor for Cabbagetown. She was well known as a lawyer and community activist. While starting out as the frontrunner in her second run for the mayoralty, she fell behind Miller and Tory by election day.

Before his first run for mayor, Tory was well known as a former federal and provincial Conservative Party insider, journalist and talk-show host, Rogers Media and Cable CEO, CFL commissioner, and lawyer. He ran on a campaign of cutting wasteful city spending while putting more cops on the street.
A lawyer, Nunziata had previously served as Liberal and independent federal MP, where he had cultivated a maverick, populist image. Before that, York borough councillor.

Miller ran successfully in 2003 and 2006, becoming the amalgamated city's second mayor. A lawyer and sometime NDP candidate, he had previously been elected to the councils of Metro Toronto and the amalgmated city. He ran on cleaning up the city, both ethically and aesthetically.

In 2006, his platform called for transit expansion, more affordable housing, gun control measures, and waterfront redevelopment.
Leaside resident and former York borough councillor and amalgamated Toronto city councillor Pitfield called for low property taxes, spending cuts, and incinerating garbage.

Longtime populist Etobicoke city councillor and son of a former provincial Conservative MPP, Rob Ford became Toronto's third mayor on a platform of "respect for taxpayers" and improving customer service.

Early in his political career, Smitherman had worked on Barbara Hall's staff and was a co-chair of her 2003 mayoral campaign. After being elected to the provincial legislature, he served as a cabinet minister and deputy premier in Dalton McGuinty's Liberal government. Projecting an image of political experience did not translate into electoral success, and he consistently polled behind Rob Ford throughout the campaign.

A former councillor in pre-amalgamation and post-amalgamation Toronto and also at the Metro level, Pantalone served as deputy mayor under David Miller. He represented west-central neighbourhoods, including Little Italy, throughout his career. His platform represented continuity with Miller's policy legacies.

An Etobicoke businessman, Doug Ford had succeeded his brother Rob as ward councillor. When Rob Ford fell ill, Doug Ford replaced his brother as mayoral candidate at the nomination deadline. He ran on a populist, back-to-basics platform.

Artist, activist, former Metro councillor, city councillor, and federal NDP MP with deep roots in Toronto's Hong Kong Chinese community, Chow was the widow of former federal NDP leader and municipal polician Jack Layton. She ran on a platform of surface transit expansion, creating youth employment opportunities, and funding after-school recreation programs.

Tory was elected the amalgamated Toronto's fourth mayor on a centrist platform after an unsuccessful tenure as provincial Conservative leader and serving as chair of CivicAction. Keesmaat is an urban planner with substantial experience in the private sector. She served as chief planner of Toronto under Ford and Tory between 2012 and 2017. Her unsuccessful campaign focused on transit expansion, housing affordability, and road safety.

Originally from Colombia, Peñalosa has for may years been a Toronto-based urban policy consultant, and founder of the non-profit 8 80 Cities.
Brown is a policy analyst and former member of the Toronto Youth Cabinet. After Olivia Chow, she is the second female candidate of colour to receive more than 5% of the citywide vote.

Artist, activist, former Metro councillor, city councillor, and federal NDP MP with deep roots in Toronto's Hong Kong Chinese community, Chow ran unsuccessfully for mayor in 2014. In the 2023 by-election that followed John Tory's resignation, she won a crowded race on a platform of affordable housing, transit service, and investment in community services.

Born in Portugal, Bailão represented the west-end Davenport ward on city council from 2010 to 2022 and served as deputy mayor under John Tory, focusing on housing. Endorsed by Tory late in the campaign, she finished a close second.
Toronto's police chief from 2015 to 2020 and an unsuccessful provincial Progressive Conservative candidate in 2022, Saunders ran on a platform centred on public safety and fiscal restraint.
A Toronto Sun columnist and broadcaster, Furey ran a conservative, law-and-order campaign that gained ground in the final weeks of the race.
A former school board trustee, Matlow has represented midtown Toronto on city council since 2010. He ran on a progressive platform that included a new property tax levy to fund city services.

Artist, activist, former Metro councillor, city councillor, and federal NDP MP with deep roots in Toronto's Hong Kong Chinese community, Chow ran unsuccessfully for mayor in 2014 before winning the 2023 by-election. In 2026 she was re-elected in a two-way race against Brad Bradford.
A former city planner, Bradford was first elected city councillor for Beaches–East York in 2018. After a minor run in the 2023 by-election, he emerged as Chow's principal challenger in 2026.
